record.Description: This recall involves CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes. The costumes include a blue dress with a crown and wand that light up, and a remote control. The crowns, scepters, and remote controls contain button batteries. There are no markings on the product. The package has “CIYTI’ on the front.
record.Title: FoShanShiNanHaiQuNuoAiTongZhuangShangHang Recalls CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys

Images.Caption: Recalled Light Up Princess Costume and Accessories

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Amazon from February 2025 through June 2025 for between $21 and $35.

Hazards.Name: The costumes violate the mandatory safety standard for toys because the button cell batteries can be accessed easily by children, posing a deadly ingestion hazard. If button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, including internal chemical burns, and death.

Remedies.Name:
Consumers should take the princess costumes away from children immediately, stop using them and contact FoShanShiNanHaiQuNuoAiTongZhuangShangHang for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to write “RECALLED” with permanent marker on the dress, crown, wand, and remote, then throw away the toys and submit a photo of the disposed toys to Norakid2026@outlook.com.  

Note: Button cell batteries are hazardous. Batteries should be disposed of or recycled by following local hazardous waste procedures.

ai.summary: CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes have been recalled because children can easily access the button cell batteries inside the accessories and remote control. Swallowing these batteries can cause severe internal chemical burns or even death, which violates mandatory safety standards for toys.
ai.next_steps: Immediately take the costume away from children and stop using it. To receive a full refund, write “RECALLED” in permanent marker on the dress, crown, wand, and remote, discard the toys, and email a photo of the disposed items to Norakid2026@outlook.com. Follow local hazardous waste procedures when recycling or disposing of the button cell batteries.
